tagline: A tiny coding agent — 80% of the useful loop, 20% of the machinery.
starters: What's the difference between Safe and Fast?
How do I pick a model?

topics.title: Getting started
topics.body:
## Getting started

1. Run `picogent gui` once after install.
2. Tap **Select folder** and open the project you want edited.
3. If you see **Log in**, tap it — Picogent opens the browser or Terminal for you.
4. Type what you want in the chat bar — e.g. “fix the failing tests”.
5. In **Safe** mode, Picogent asks before writing files or running shell.

You should not need the Terminal again after the install one-liner. Provider logins are started from the **Log in** button in chat or Settings.

topics.title: Safe vs Fast
topics.blurb: Permission modes in the top bar.
topics.body:
## Safe vs Fast

Use the **Safe / Fast** toggle in the top bar.

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Safe** (default) | Asks before writes and shell commands |
| **Fast** | Auto-edits inside the workspace; still asks for deletes, `rm`, and paths outside the folder |

When a permission prompt appears, you can **Deny**, allow for **This turn**, **Always allow**, or **Allow** once.

Tip: stay in Safe while exploring a new repo; switch to Fast when you trust the loop.

topics.title: Models & Auto
topics.blurb: The Auto picker next to Send.
topics.body:
## Models & Auto

The **Auto** control next to the send button picks which model runs.

- **Auto** lets Picogent route the task (light vs heavy models when available).
- Pick a specific model to lock the turn to that choice.

Providers live in **Settings**: Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode (Zen/Go), Antigravity.

If a provider needs login, tap **Log in** — Picogent opens the browser or Terminal for you. You should not type login commands yourself.

topics.title: Chat & attachments
topics.blurb: Message bar, files, and streaming replies.
topics.body:
## Chat & attachments

- Type in **Message Picogent** and press Enter (Shift+Enter for a new line).
- Use **+** to attach images, PDFs, and code/text files.
- Replies stream live and render **Markdown** and **LaTeX** (`$...$`, `$$...$$`) as they arrive.
- Click `path:line` citations in a reply to open the Review panel.

The spinning ring on the chat bar means a turn is in progress. You can still type; send queues a follow-up where supported.

topics.title: Slash commands
topics.body:
## Slash commands

Type `/` in the chat bar to open the command menu.

Built-ins include:
- `/commit` — prepare a commit
- `/review` — review changes
- `/clear` — reset the chat
- `/status` — session status
- `/diff` — show git diff
- `/compact` — shrink context
- `/memory` — project rules + learned habits/playbooks
- `/agent` `/ask` `/plan` `/debug` — task modes
- `/goal …` — set or clear a goal

**Custom commands:** add `.claude/commands/deploy.md` in your project, then type `/deploy`.

topics.title: Review & changes
topics.body:
## Review & changes

Open the **Review** icon in the top-right.

- **Review** — file lines Picogent read or cited (`path:line`)
- **Changes** — edits with added/removed line counts; click a file to jump in
- **Activity** — tool and turn events for this workspace

Ask about a line from the review footer (“Line 42 or ask about this file”).

topics.title: MCP & extensions
topics.body:
## MCP & extensions

Ask in chat to connect GitHub, a browser, or search — Picogent uses `mcp_manage` and waits for Allow in Safe mode.

Config is Cursor-compatible and loaded only from user-owned locations:
1. `~/.cursor/mcp.json`
2. `~/.picogent/mcp.yaml`

Workspace `.cursor/mcp.json` and `.mcp.json` files are never autoloaded: connecting a server can run a command or contact an endpoint before its tools can ask for permission.

`picogent mcp list` shows connected tools. Manage installed extensions under **Settings → Extensions**.

topics.title: Project rules
topics.body:
## Project rules

Drop `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in your repo. Picogent injects them into the system prompt (same idea as Claude Code).

Use them for house style, test commands, “never touch X”, and repo-specific conventions.

topics.title: Self-evolution
topics.body:
## Self-evolution

Picogent is already your assistant — you do not command it to “be helpful.” After meaningful turns it quietly remembers:

- **Habits** — short preferences (how you like tests run, style, safety)
- **Playbooks** — tiny reusable procedures for a class of task

These live in `~/.picogent/evolve/` and load into the next turn automatically, with a **hard prompt budget (≤720 chars)** and relevance filtering so self-evolution never erases Picogent’s TokenTamer / soft-budget savings. Reflection is **heuristic by default** (zero extra model tokens); set `PICOGENT_EVOLVE_LLM=1` only if you want a light-model review.

You will see a short line like “Remembered — habit: …” when something new sticks.

Inspired by Hermes Agent’s skill + curator ideas, but kept tiny: no separate evolution CLI, no DSPy stack, no PR workflow.

Use `/memory` to peek at project rules plus what Picogent has learned.

topics.title: Context bar
topics.body:
## Context window

Codex models get a **256k** hard ceiling. Picogent does **not** try to fill it.

Every tool round runs soft compaction (TokenTamer + digests + soft-fit) so the live working set stays near a small soft target and the ring grows slowly — Cursor-style headroom, not a race to the limit.

When pressure still climbs, older turns are windowed or summarized. You can also run `/compact`.

topics.title: CLI cheatsheet
topics.body:
## CLI cheatsheet

```
picogent              # TUI (setup on first run)
picogent gui          # browser chat
picogent setup        # open setup again
picogent login        # Codex
picogent login claude # Claude Code
picogent run --yes "…"  # one-shot, Fast-ish
picogent init --ollama
picogent mcp          # list MCP tools
picogent version
```

Useful flags: `--dir PATH`, `--yes`, `--model NAME`.
